summary: StateReporting lets an app define named domains, report one active state per domain and attach reportable metadata, so that MetricKit and Instruments can attribute crashes and metrics to app state. BifrOSt has no app-facing state-transition or metadata API. Its system layer captures crash.log entries, offers a Share with Developer action and unified logging; these cover the diagnostics side but not the state attribution.

features.note: Wave 2 (statereporting, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no SDK type records a named domain or a single active state per domain; the log module only writes messages

lists crash logs, Share with Developer, Delete All Crash Logs; the share uploads build, crash logs and heartbeat to the update server

features.note: Logger and LogStore exist; no info-in-memory tier, no per-value privacy masks (docs/bifrost-ui.md, Unified Logging)

features.feature: Points of Interest and signposts for Instruments
features.apple: OSSignposter (interval and event marks shown beside state transitions)
features.note: Wave 2 (statereporting, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. docs/bifrost-ui.md states no OSSignposter exists yet

features.apple: MetricKit metric entries that carry state context
features.note: MetricKit is Apple's delivery service for the metrics; BifrOSt has no equivalent metric payload for apps, and the performance HUD sensor readings in diag.rs are not app-facing

gaps: No app-facing StateReporter: apps cannot declare domains or report state transitions.
No reportable-metadata type or derive macro for attaching structured values to reports.
No signposter (OSSignposter equivalent) for marking intervals and events in traces.
Crash logs are not linked to app state; a crash carries only a signature and file path (springboard/src/shell/diag.rs).
No app-facing metric payload delivered to the developer comparable to MetricKit.
